record.title: Available Guardrails quantifies when selective prediction can be certified
record.summary: The September 2026 Available Guardrails preprint studies whether finite calibration data can certify target precision for every reporting unit in a selective prediction system. It uses exact-binomial inversion and dynamic programming to expose the trade-off among certified precision, subgroup granularity and served traffic. In author-run evaluations, split-sample partition selection gains a reported mean 0.060 coverage over support balancing, with a positive direction in 59 of 60 model effects across three intent-routing datasets and two architectures; a naive estimator captures only 0.005 of a reported 0.157 population-known opportunity.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports that truth-informed planning gains 0.157 mean coverage over support balancing, while a naive estimator recovers 0.005. Selecting among candidate partitions on a separate split gains a mean 0.060 over support balancing, with the direction reproduced in 59 of 60 model effects across three intent-routing datasets and two architectures. Additional application settings include tool calling, content moderation, lesion classification and recommendation.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv record identifies the paper and its submission/revision metadata. This confirms that the preprint was posted, not that its experimental claims have been independently established.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the PDF Tables 1–3 or the reported 59/60 direction count was inspected.
No deployment-shift test or evaluation of whether the certified outcome matches real harm was inspected.

brief.importance_rationale: If the results hold, treating certificate availability as a deployment resource could materially change how selective safety gates are partitioned and evaluated across tools and user groups. The evidence is an author-run statistical study; its results do not show that a certified gate captures the relevant harm or remains valid under distribution shift.
limitations: All quantitative findings are author-reported; no independent reproduction was inspected.
The 0.060 coverage gain is reported for the paper’s candidate-generation and split-selection procedure; the abstract reports direction in 59 of 60 model effects, while individual magnitudes vary.
The method fixes a group order; adaptive or unconstrained partition search creates additional selection and multiple-testing concerns.
A certificate under the calibration distribution does not establish validity under distribution shift, and a statistical precision label may omit the harm that matters in deployment.

technical.claimed_result: The paper reports that truth-informed planning gains 0.157 mean coverage over support balancing, while a naive estimator recovers 0.005. technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv preprint and its method/experimental design were inspected. The numerical outcome is reported by the paper authors and is not independently demonstrated in this review.
technical.mechanism: The authors compute exact-binomial precision certificates and use dynamic programming to select reporting partitions under a fixed group order. They then evaluate split-sample selection and familywise error-budget allocation as ways to improve certified availability from finite data.
technical.regime: Author-run finite-sample and population-quantity analyses of selective prediction, including three intent-routing datasets and two architectures for the 60-effect direction count; additional cross-domain gate applications are reported in the preprint.
technical.strongest_baseline: Support balancing, a naive estimator and split-sample candidate partition selection under the paper’s fixed group-order assumptions; reported 0.060 mean-coverage gain is not an independent reproduction.

brief.title: Available Guardrails quantifies when selective prediction can be certified
brief.why_it_matters: A safety gate can have strong precision among allowed outputs while being unable to certify some groups or tools at all. Measuring availability alongside precision and coverage helps expose the amount of deployment surface the evidence actually supports, while preserving the distinction between statistical certification and real-world safety.
